finalText:
Migration finished. 250 exported functions exercised at runtime produced 225 database calls, all on the new form, and zero on `query`.

**Migrated — 36 call sites across 12 files** (the last stragglers under `packages/`):

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `service/teamService.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |

Each `db.query(sql, params)` became `db.execute({ sql, params })`, matching the 63 files migrated in earlier passes byte-for-byte in shape — I diffed the three file archetypes (repo/admin/service) against their already-migrated peers and they're structurally identical. All 78 files pass `node --check`.

**Two things I deliberately did not change:**

1. **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js`** still has 2 `db.query` calls (lines 9 and 13). Its header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, "replaced wholesale on every upgrade, and local changes are silently lost" — so editing it would be undone by the next bump while making the tree look done. Since `lib/db.js` says the driver's next major *drops* `query`, this is a real remaining exposure that needs a different fix: upgrade the vendored lib, or shim it at the require boundary (pass the adapter a wrapper that maps positional args onto `execute`). Worth a ticket; I didn't want to pick that direction for you.

2. **`cache.query(...)` — 25 files.** Despite the matching name, `lib/cache.js` takes a cache key rather than SQL and is unrelated to the db handle; the already-migrated files keep these calls as-is. A plain find-and-replace on `.query(` would have silently broken every read-through cache lookup in the repo.
